text: You could stand here, in Antarctica, and see no ice at all.
The story goes, it hasn't rained here in 2 million years.
This valley sits beside the biggest ice sheet on Earth.
They wall off the glaciers trying to flow in.
Then, the wind finishes the job.
Freezing air pours off the ice sheet, warms as it drops, and scours the valleys, with
gusts measured near 140 kilometers an hour.
Snow doesn't stand a chance. Some snow does fall, about 10 centimeters a year.
But this air is so dry, the snow turns straight into vapor. In summer, it can vanish in hours.
So, nothing here gets wet. Nothing rots, either. Seals that wandered inland lie freeze-dried.
Some may be 2,000 years old. Cold? Dry? Dead-looking? Sound familiar? NASA thought so.
Scientists have tested Mars ideas here since the Viking missions of the 1970s.
Because the closest thing to Mars isn't in space, it's at the bottom of our own planet.
Here's the twist, life still made it here, hiding inside the rocks.
No rain, no rent, great view.
